- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.  
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–5% from forecast for 2–3 periods post-spike.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce forecast toward historical mean unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use sentiment lag (e.g., 3–5 day average) to smooth out noisy signals before forecasting.  
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit recent moves; use 10-day moving average as a baseline for correction.
